observations.seen: The night pitch in frames 1 and 2 is lit unevenly, with dark blotches across the grass and no clear floodlight pools. The sand court in frame 3 is lit by one flat warm key that gives the players little form.
Each player casts a long soft directional shadow and also has a round blob shadow at the feet. In frame 3 the blob reads as a separate dark disc rather than contact shading.

In frame 4 the blue floor shows faint mirrored player reflections and a large white specular hotspot at the lower right. In frame 2 the grass has noisy specular sparkle that reads as wet plastic instead of turf.

The crowd is rows of identical capsule billboards with stray white spheres. The same arrangement repeats in frames 1, 3 and 4. The stands are flat dark or orange boxes, and the only structural detail is one light truss in frame 2.
No indoor haze, light shafts or depth falloff is visible. Frame 4 has only a slight blue wash toward the stands.

The grass texture is smeared and swirled with high-frequency noise and streaks, so it reads as distorted rather than mown turf. The sand court in frame 3 is an untextured flat beige. The line paint is clean but has no surface variation.
The players are simple stylized low-poly figures with readable kits, and the goal and net in frame 2 are serviceable. The capsule crowd and box stands are placeholder-level.
The kickoff frames are centered on the circle with both teams spread evenly, but the top 30% of the frame is the repeating crowd strip. Frame 2 has a better diagonal toward the goal.
A high perspective broadcast angle is used instead of the orthographic 70° recipe. It reads well, but the near pitch edge fills a lot of the frame with empty grass.
Frame 4 has a heavy vignette and a blown bloom hotspot that looks like an artifact. The grass shimmer in frames 1 and 2 suggests temporal or denoise smearing. No color grade ties the venues together.
Frame 2 shows plausible mid-stride running poses. The kickoff frames show stiff, identical idle stances with arms at the sides.

nextChange.change: add the recipe row's atmosphere (fog scale, haze, shafts) at the look's intensity
